findings.text: follow-on: the fragment says the sample was 'drawn at random within each source category', but the run's build_sample.py draws a deterministic stride (ids[::step]) from an id-sorted list, so the artifact misstates its own sampling method.

follow-on: the fragment says 'All 202 are grouped catalogue members' and reprocess-sample-ids.json records all_grouped_members true with grouped_members_in_sample 202 (any MEMBER_OF member), while reprocess.html:65 calls only the 17 whose source carries more than one member the 'grouped members'; one term carries two counts in one artifact, and the done-when's 'each sampled grouped member' is shown for 17, not 202.

follow-on: the declared negative control's receipt is asserted ('A census taken immediately after the reset found 202 of the sample's signals at discovered and 0 with a description') but no captured output records that census; the run's only captured census output is the post-enrichment one at 12:04:17Z.

follow-on: the done-when requires reprocess.html to record the reprocess start, but the fragment only refers to 'the reprocess start' without the instant (2026-10-13T11:53:35Z), which lives only in the sibling JSON.

follow-on: test_logs cites reset2.log and enrich1.log under the run directory, where neither file exists; the logs live only on node-local scratch (/tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261013T113938701940-ssfms-reprocess-sample/), which dies with the allocation, so a later reader cannot open the cited evidence.
